translations.literal: I pray that Your Majesty reverse your decision and execute Yanze to appease the military staff."）〉
translations.idiomatic: I pray that Your Majesty reverse your judgment and execute Yanze to satisfy the army staff."）〉

sentences.zh: 戊辰，廢雄州為昌化軍，警州為威肅軍，其軍使委本道差補。

translations.literal: On the wuchen day, Xiongzhou was abolished as Changhua Army and Jingzhou as Weisu Army; their army commissioners were to be appointed by their respective circuits.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Xiongzhou was reduced to Changhua Army and Jingzhou to Weisu Army, with army commissioners to be appointed by their circuits.

sentences.zh: 故涇州節度掌書記張式贈尚書虞部郎中，以式父鐸為沁州司馬致仕，弟守貞為貝州清河縣主簿，男希範為興元府文學。

translations.literal: Zhang Shi, former secretary of the Jingzhou military administration, was posthumously granted Director in the Ministry of Works, Yu Bureau; Shi's father Duo was made Sima of Qinzhou with retired status; his younger brother Shouzhen was made secretary of Qinghe County in Beizhou; and his son Xifan was made literary officer at Xingyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Former Jingzhou military secretary Zhang Shi was posthumously made Director in the Ministry of Works, Yu Bureau. His father Duo was made retired Sima of Qinzhou, his brother Shouzhen secretary of Qinghe County in Beizhou, and his son Xifan literary officer at Xingyuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，詔皇子齊王就前河中府節度使康福第，以教坊樂宴會前、見任節度使。

translations.literal: On the jiaxu day, an edict ordered the prince, Prince of Qi, to go to the residence of Kang Fu, former military commissioner of the Hezhong prefecture, and with music-bureau entertainment hold a banquet for current and former military commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, the emperor ordered Prince of Qi to visit the residence of former Hezhong commissioner Kang Fu and, with music-bureau entertainment, host current and former military commissioners.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，前慶州刺史米廷訓追奪在身官爵，配流麟州，坐奸妻兄之女也。

translations.literal: On the wuyin day, Mi Tingxun, former prefect of Qingzhou, was stripped of all active offices and ranks and banished to Linzhou for having committed adultery with his wife's brother's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, former Qingzhou prefect Mi Tingxun was stripped of rank and banished to Linzhou for adultery with his wife's brother's daughter.

sentences.zh: 是月，州郡十六處蝗。

translations.literal: That month, locusts appeared in sixteen prefectures and districts.
translations.idiomatic: That month locusts struck sixteen prefectures.

sentences.zh: 五月己亥，中書門下奏：「時屬炎蒸，事宜簡省。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the jihai day, the Chancellery memorialized: "The season is one of oppressive heat, and affairs should be simplified.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai in the fifth month, the Chancellery reported: "The season is oppressively hot, and court business should be simplified.

sentences.zh: 應五日百官起居，望令押班宰臣一員押百官班，其轉對官兩員封付閣門使引進，本官隨百僚退，不用別出謝恩。

translations.literal: For the officials' audience every five days, it is requested that one leading grand councilor lead the officials' formation; the two rotating remonstrance officials should have their sealed memorials delivered to the Gate Department commissioners for presentation, and the officials themselves should withdraw with the hundred ranks without separately coming out to express thanks.
translations.idiomatic: For the five-day imperial audience, one leading grand councilor should lead the officials' formation. The two rotating remonstrance officials' sealed memorials should be delivered to the Gate Department commissioners for presentation, and those officials should withdraw with the rest without a separate audience of thanks.

sentences.zh: 其文武內外官僚乞假、寧覲、搬家、婚葬、病損並門見門辭。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials within and outside the court who request leave, visit parents, move house, marry, bury, or fall ill should all report at the gate when leaving and when returning.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials inside and outside the court seeking leave, parental visits, moves, weddings, funerals, or sick leave should all report at the gate on departure and return.

sentences.zh: 諸道進奉物等，不用殿前排列，引進使引至殿前奏云『某等進奉』，奏訖，令進奉使便出。

translations.literal: Tribute items from the various circuits need not be lined up before the hall; the reception commissioners should lead them before the hall, where they report, "We present tribute," and after the report the tribute envoys may withdraw at once.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit tribute need not be lined up before the hall. Reception commissioners should lead envoys forward to announce, "We present tribute," after which the tribute envoys may withdraw at once.

sentences.zh: 其進奉專使朝見日，班首一人致詞，都附起居。

translations.literal: On the day the special tribute envoys attend audience, the leader of the formation alone should speak; all are attached to the routine audience.
translations.idiomatic: When tribute envoys attend audience, only the formation leader should speak, and all are attached to the routine audience.

sentences.zh: 刺史並行軍副使、諸道馬步軍都指揮使已下，差人到闕，並門見門辭。

translations.literal: Prefects, deputy military commissioners, and commanders of horse and foot armies of the various circuits and below who send men to court should all report at the gate when leaving and when returning.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects, deputy military commissioners, and circuit horse-and-foot commanders who send representatives to court should report at the gate on departure and return.

sentences.zh: 州縣官謝恩日，甲頭一人都致詞，不用逐人告官。

translations.literal: On the day county and prefecture officials express thanks, one lead official alone should speak; there is no need for each person to announce his office.
translations.idiomatic: When county and prefecture officials express thanks, one lead official alone should speak; each need not announce his office separately.

sentences.zh: 其供奉官、殿直等，如是當直及合於殿前排立者，即入起居；

translations.literal: For palace service officers and hall attendants, if they are on duty and should stand in formation before the hall, they enter for the audience;
translations.idiomatic: Palace service officers and hall attendants on duty and required to stand before the hall should enter for audience;

sentences.zh: 如不當直排立者，不用每日起居。

translations.literal: if they are not on duty for hall formation, they need not attend audience daily.
translations.idiomatic: those not on duty for hall formation need not attend daily audience.

sentences.zh: 委宣徽使點檢，常須整齊。」

translations.literal: This is entrusted to the Palace Administration commissioner to inspect, and order must be maintained at all times."
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Administration commissioner is to inspect and keep order at all times."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 時帝不豫，難於視朝故也。

translations.literal: This was because the emperor was unwell and found it difficult to hold court.
translations.idiomatic: This was because the emperor was unwell and could not easily hold court.

sentences.zh: 〈（《遼史》：二月甲午，遣使使晉，索吐谷渾叛者。

translations.literal: (From the Liao History: In the second month, on the jiawu day, envoys were sent to Jin to demand Tuyuhun rebels.
translations.idiomatic: (Liao History: In the second month, on jiawu, envoys were sent to Later Jin to demand Tuyuhun rebels.

sentences.zh: 《契丹國志》云：遼以晉招納吐谷渾，遣使責讓，晉高祖憂悒成疾。）〉

translations.literal: The Khitan State Annals states: Because Liao believed Jin had harbored Tuyuhun, it sent envoys to rebuke them, and Jin Gaozu grieved himself into illness.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan State Annals states that because Liao believed Later Jin had harbored Tuyuhun, it sent envoys to rebuke the court, and Jin Gaozu grieved himself into illness.)〉

sentences.zh: 左威衛上將軍衛審餘卒，贈太子少保。

translations.literal: Wei Shenyu, Grand General of the Left Prestige Guard, died and was posthumously granted Vice Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Left Prestige Guard Grand General Wei Shenyu died and was posthumously made Vice Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，尊皇太妃劉氏為皇太后。

translations.literal: On the yisi day, Imperial Consort Liu was honored as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, Imperial Consort Liu was honored as Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 〈（徐無黨《五代史記註》云：高祖所生母也。）〉

translations.literal: (Xu Wudang's Commentary on the Historical Records of the Five Dynasties states: She was the birth mother of Gaozu.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Xu Wudang, Commentary on the Historical Records of the Five Dynasties: she was the emperor's biological mother.)〉

sentences.zh: 丁未，工部侍郎韋勛改刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: On day dingwei, Wei Xun, Vice Minister of Works, was transferred to Vice Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Works Vice Minister Wei Xun was transferred to Punishments Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 壬子，以左散騎常侍李光廷為秘書監，給事中蕭願為右散騎常侍，左諫議大夫曹國珍為給事中，太常卿裴坦為左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: On day renzi, Li Guangting, Left Attendant Cavalier, was made Director of the Imperial Library; Xiao Yuan, Attending Drafter, was made Right Attendant Cavalier; Cao Guozhen, Left Remonstrance Censor, was made Attending Drafter; Pei Tan, Minister of Ceremonial, was made Left Remonstrance Censor.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Left Attendant Cavalier Li Guangting became Imperial Library director; Attending Drafter Xiao Yuan became Right Attendant Cavalier; Left Remonstrance Censor Cao Guozhen became attending drafter; and Ceremonial Minister Pei Tan became Left Remonstrance Censor.

sentences.zh: 是月，州郡五奏大水，十八奏旱蝗。

translations.literal: That month, five prefectures and districts memorialized great floods, and eighteen memorialized drought and locusts.
translations.idiomatic: That month five jurisdictions reported major floods and eighteen reported drought and locust plagues.

sentences.zh: 六月丁巳，以兗州節度使桑維翰為晉昌軍節度使，以前許州節度使安審琦為兗州節度使。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on day dingsi, Sang Weihan, military commissioner of Yanzhou, was made military commissioner of the Jinchang army; An Shenqi, former military commissioner of Xuzhou, was made military commissioner of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on dingsi, Yanzhou commissioner Sang Weihan became Jinchang army commissioner, and former Xuzhou commissioner An Shenqi became Yanzhou commissioner.

sentences.zh: 襄州都部署高行周奏，安從進觀察判官李光圖出城請援，送赴闕。

translations.literal: Gao Xingzhou, overall commander at Xiangzhou, memorialized that Li Guangtu, observation administration judge of An Congjin, had left the city to request aid and was sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangzhou commander Gao Xingzhou reported that An Congjin's observation judge Li Guangtu had left the city seeking reinforcements and was escorted to court.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，帝崩於保昌殿，壽五十一。

translations.literal: On day yichou, the emperor died in the Baochang Hall, aged fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou the emperor died in the Baochang Hall at the age of fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 遺制齊王重貴於柩前即皇帝位，喪紀並依舊制，山陵務從節儉，馬步諸軍優紀並從嗣君處分。

translations.literal: His final edict installed Chonggui, Prince of Qi, as emperor before the coffin; mourning rites were to follow the old regulations; the imperial tomb was to be kept frugal; and preferential treatment for the horse and foot armies was left to the disposition of the succeeding ruler.
translations.idiomatic: His deathbed edict installed Prince Chonggui of Qi as emperor before the coffin. Mourning was to follow established custom, the tomb was to be kept austere, and rewards for the armies were left to the new emperor's discretion.

sentences.zh: 〈（《通鑒考異》云：《漢高祖實錄》：晉高祖大漸，召近臣屬之曰：「此天下，明宗之天下，寡人竊而處之久矣。

translations.literal: (Examination of Variants in the Comprehensive Mirror states: The Veritable Record of Han Gaozu records that as Later Jin Gaozu lay gravely ill, he summoned close ministers and entrusted them, saying: "This realm is the realm of Emperor Mingzong; I have held it in usurpation for long.
translations.idiomatic: (Examination of Variants in the Comprehensive Mirror: According to the Veritable Record of Han Gaozu, as Later Jin Gaozu lay dying he summoned his inner circle and said, "This realm belongs to Emperor Mingzong; I have held it only by usurpation for many years.

sentences.zh: 寡人既謝，當歸許王，寡人之願也。」

translations.literal: When I depart, it should return to the Prince of Xu—that is my wish."
translations.idiomatic: When I am gone, it should return to the Prince of Xu. That is my wish."

sentences.zh: 此說難信。）〉

translations.literal: This account is hard to credit.)〉
translations.idiomatic: This account is difficult to credit.)〉

sentences.zh: 八月，太常卿崔棁上謚曰聖文章武明德孝皇帝，廟號高祖。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Cui Zhuo, Minister of Ceremonial, submitted the posthumous title Emperor Shengwen Zhangwu Mingde Xiao, with temple name Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Ceremonial Minister Cui Zhuo proposed the posthumous title Emperor Shengwen Zhangwu Mingde Xiao, with the temple name Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 以其年十一月十日庚寅葬於顯陵，宰臣和凝撰謚冊哀冊文。

translations.literal: On the gengyin day, the tenth day of the eleventh month of that year, he was buried at the Xian Mausoleum; Grand Councilor He Ning composed the texts for the posthumous patent and lamentation volumes.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, the tenth day of the eleventh month of that year, he was buried at the Xian Mausoleum. Grand Councilor He Ning drafted the posthumous patent and lamentation texts.

sentences.zh: 〈（《五代史補》：高祖尚明宗女，宮中謂之石郎。

translations.literal: (Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: Gaozu married a daughter of Emperor Mingzong, and within the palace he was called Lord Stone.
translations.idiomatic: (Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: Gaozu married Emperor Mingzong's daughter and was known in the palace as Lord Stone.

sentences.zh: 及將起兵於太原，京師夜間狼皆群走，往往入宮中，湣帝患之，命諸班能射者分頭捕逐，謂之「射狼」。

translations.literal: When he was about to raise troops at Taiyuan, at night in the capital wolves all ran in packs, often entering the palace. Emperor Min was troubled and ordered skilled archers of the various guard shifts to hunt them separately, calling it "shooting the wolves."
translations.idiomatic: When he was preparing to raise troops at Taiyuan, wolves ran in packs through the capital at night and often entered the palace. Emperor Min, alarmed, ordered the best archers in each guard shift to hunt them down, calling the operation "wolf-shooting."

sentences.zh: 或遇諸塗，問曰：「汝何從而來？」

translations.literal: If one met others on the road, they would ask, "Where have you come from?"
translations.idiomatic: People meeting on the road would ask, "Where are you coming from?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「看射狼。」

translations.literal: The reply was, "To watch the wolf-shooting."
translations.idiomatic: The answer was, "To watch the wolf-shooting."

sentences.zh: 未幾，高祖至。

translations.literal: Before long, Gaozu arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Gaozu arrived.

sentences.zh: 蓋「射」韻「石」相近也。

translations.literal: For the rhyme of "shoot" is close to that of "stone."
translations.idiomatic: For the rhyme of "shoot" (she) was close to that of "stone" (shi).

sentences.zh: 《五代史闕文》：梁開平初，潞州行營使李思安奏：函關縣穰鄉民伐樹，樹仆，自分為二，中有六字如左書，云「天十四載石進」，梁帝藏於武庫，時莫詳其義。

translations.literal: Lost Texts of the History of the Five Dynasties: At the beginning of Kaiping in Liang, Li Si'an, field commissioner at Luzhou, memorialized that in Rang township, Hanguan County, villagers felled a tree; when it fell it split in two of itself, and within were six characters written like script to the left, reading "Heaven's fourteenth year, Stone advances." Emperor of Liang stored it in the armory, and at the time none could explain its meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Lost Texts of the History of the Five Dynasties: Early in Liang's Kaiping era, Luzhou field commissioner Li Si'an reported that in Rang township, Hanguan County, villagers felled a tree that split in two as it fell. Inside were six characters reading, "Heaven's fourteenth year, Stone advances." The Liang emperor placed it in the armory, and no one then understood its meaning.

sentences.zh: 至帝即位，識者曰：「『天』字取『四』字兩畫加之於傍，即『丙』字也；

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, those who understood said, "Take the character 'four' and add its two strokes beside 'heaven,' and you have the character 'bing';
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, interpreters said, "add the two strokes of 'four' beside 'heaven' and you get 'bing';

sentences.zh: 『四』字去中之兩畫加『十』字，即『申』字也。

translations.literal: remove the two inner strokes of "four" and add "ten," and you have the character "shen."
translations.idiomatic: remove the inner strokes of "four" and add "ten" and you get "shen."

sentences.zh: 帝即位之年，乃『丙申』也。

translations.literal: The year the emperor took the throne was indeed "bingshen."
translations.idiomatic: The year of his enthronement was indeed "bingshen."

sentences.zh: 進者晉也，石者姓也。」

translations.literal: Advances means Jin, and 'Stone' is the surname."
translations.idiomatic: Advances meant Jin, and 'Stone' was the surname."

sentences.zh: 臣謹按，天祐二十年，歲在癸未，其年莊宗建號，改同光元年，至清泰三年，歲丙申，其年晉祖即位，改元天福元年，自未至申，凡十四載矣，故讖書云「天十四載石進」者，言自天祐滅後十四載石氏興於晉也，豈不明乎！

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully notes: In the twentieth year of Tianyou, the year was in guiwei; that year Zhuangzong established his reign title and changed to the first year of Tongguang. By the third year of Qingtai, the year was bingshen; that year the Jin ancestor took the throne and changed the era to the first year of Tianfu. From wei to shen was fourteen years in all. Thus the prophecy's words "Heaven's fourteenth year, Stone advances" mean that fourteen years after the end of Tianyou the Shi clan rose in Jin—is this not clear!
translations.idiomatic: This chronicler respectfully observes: Tianyou 20 fell in guiwei, the year Zhuangzong proclaimed his reign and renamed the era Tongguang 1. By Qingtai 3, in bingshen, the Jin founder took the throne and proclaimed Tianfu 1. From wei to shen was exactly fourteen years. Thus the prophecy "Heaven's fourteenth year, Stone advances" means that fourteen years after Tianyou's end the Shi clan rose in Jin—is that not plain!

sentences.zh: 而拆字解讖以就丙申，非也。）〉

translations.literal: Yet to split characters and force the prophecy to fit bingshen is wrong.)〉
translations.idiomatic: But to dissect the characters and force the prophecy to fit bingshen is mistaken.)〉

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：晉祖潛躍之前沈毅而已。

translations.literal: The historiographer states: Before the Jin ancestor's hidden rise, he was merely steady and resolute.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Before Gaozu's rise, he was known chiefly for steadiness and resolve.

sentences.zh: 及其為君也，旰食宵衣，禮賢從諫，慕黃、老之教，樂清凈之風，以絁為衣，以麻為履，故能保其社稷，高朗令終。

translations.literal: When he became ruler, he toiled from dawn and worked late into the night, honored the worthy and heeded remonstrance, admired the teachings of Huangdi and Laozi, delighted in the spirit of purity and quiet, wore coarse silk for garments and hemp for shoes, and thus was able to preserve his altars of soil and grain and end his reign in lofty clarity.
translations.idiomatic: As emperor he rose early and worked late, honored worthies and accepted remonstrance, cherished the teachings of the Yellow Emperor and Laozi, loved simplicity and restraint, wore coarse silk and hemp sandals, and so preserved the realm and ended his reign in dignity.

sentences.zh: 然而圖事之初，召戎來援，獫狁自茲而孔熾，黔黎由是以罹殃。

translations.literal: Yet at the beginning of his plotting he summoned the Rong for aid; from then the Xianyun grew fiercely rampant, and the black-haired people thereby suffered calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in seeking power he called in the barbarians; from that moment the northern tribes grew dangerously strong, and the common people bore the cost.

sentences.zh: 迨至嗣君，兵連禍結，卒使都城失守，舉族為俘。

translations.literal: By the time of the succeeding ruler, war linked with disaster, until at last the capital fell and the whole clan was taken captive.
translations.idiomatic: Under his successor war and disaster compounded until the capital fell and the entire clan was taken captive.

sentences.zh: 亦猶決鯨海以救焚，何逃沒溺；

translations.literal: It was like breaching the whale seas to extinguish a fire—how could one escape drowning;
translations.idiomatic: It was like breaching the ocean to fight a fire—drowning was inevitable;

sentences.zh: 飲鴆漿而止渴，終取喪亡。

translations.literal: or drinking poison to quench thirst—ruin was the final result.
translations.idiomatic: or drinking poison to slake thirst—ruin was the only end.

sentences.zh: 謀之不臧，何至於是！

translations.literal: His plans were ill-considered—how did it come to this!
translations.idiomatic: Ill-conceived policy—how could it end otherwise!

sentences.zh: 倘使非由外援之力，自副皇天之命，以茲睿德，惠彼蒸民，雖未足以方駕前王，亦可謂仁慈恭儉之主也。

translations.literal: Had he not relied on the power of foreign aid, had he himself matched Heaven's mandate, and with such sagely virtue benefited the black-haired people, though he might not have equaled the former kings, he could still have been called a ruler of benevolence, reverence, and frugality.
translations.idiomatic: Had he not depended on foreign arms, had he truly borne Heaven's mandate, and with such wisdom cared for the people, he might not have rivaled the greatest of antiquity, yet he could still have been remembered as a benevolent, reverent, and frugal sovereign.
